newsitem.title: FRANCE: French employers call for further rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: French employers call for further rate cuts.

text.p: France's employers' association called on Wednesday for further interest rate cuts to help companies adjust to a drop in producer prices.

"These elements argue for going further in the reduction of interest rates, vital to help companies in this difficult period of adjustment in their prices," Denis Kessler, vice-president of the CNPF and head of its economics committee, said in an editorial in the association's regular newsletter.
"The drop in producer prices in many sectors, industrial or not, creates a new situation which is disturbing economists and participants in the economy," Kessler wrote.
"Thus, growth in production volume is not stopping a fall in turnover of many companies."
Kessler said companies lack incentive to raise inventories or invest because falling prices make it advantageous to wait.

"Even if the cost of funds falls because of the drop in interest rates, it (a company) has no reason to raise inventories if inventories of intermediate and finished goods lose value because of the drop in prices," Kessler said.
Kessler added that companies also lack incentive to invest as long as internal return on investment projects falls because of a drop in the actualised value of its cashflow.
This behaviour largely explains a sharp fall in stocks and weak investment growth.

"As long as the market has not found its price balance -- and there are more downward adjustments to be made in certain industries -- the fall in interest rates and the improvement in outlook that we have seen over the last two months will not have their effect on stock building and investment," Kessler said.
